scorecards.inningsCommentary: Bangladesh commenced their first innings at Seddon Park, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 126 from Tamim Iqbal, complemented by a commanding 64-run stand between Mominul Haque and Tamim Iqbal that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.94 RPO. New Zealand's bowling response was spearheaded by Neil Wagner (5/47), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 234/10 (59.2 ov), Bangladesh posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: New Zealand began their reply under scoreboard pressure, tasked with responding to Bangladesh's opening innings total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 200 from Kane Williamson, complemented by a commanding 254-run stand between JA Raval and Tom Latham that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.37 RPO. Soumya Sarkar (2/67) maintained tight lines for Bangladesh, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 715/6 (162.6 ov), New Zealand's innings completed the first-innings exchange (481 Runs (New Zealand)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Bangladesh sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 149 from Soumya Sarkar, complemented by a commanding 235-run stand between Mohammad Mahmudullah and Soumya Sarkar that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.12 RPO. New Zealand's bowling response was spearheaded by Trent Boult (5/119), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Bangladesh's total of 429/10 (102.6 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Seddon Park commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 234/10 (59.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 715/6 (162.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Soumya Sarkar 149 (172b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Tamim Iqbal delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (200 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 57%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by Kane Williamson (200 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by innings & 52 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
